Hidasi and Czapp (2023) identify negative-candidate sampling as an evaluation flaw: it inflates ranking scores and can reverse model comparisons. Krichene and Rendle (2020) show that reversals can persist even in expectation; repeated sampling reduces noise but cannot recover the full-catalog objective automatically. [Hidasi–Czapp](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf), [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

Mathematically, with N eligible candidates including the target, target rank r, and 99 uniformly sampled unique negatives, sampled HR@10 has expectation P(X≤9), where X follows Hypergeometric(N−1, r−1, 99), assuming consistent tie handling. Thus a large sampled/full-catalog gap is expected and alone diagnoses neither a bug nor a particular model weakness. Useful additional information comes from paired target-rank distributions across models, categories and user/item strata: one model may achieve more true top-10 placements while another moves more targets into moderately good ranks rewarded by sampling. Pointwise rank dominance cannot reverse in expectation under identical sampling conditions; crossing rank distributions can. These are deductions from the sampling model, consistent with the published inconsistency analysis. [Rank-distribution analysis](https://arxiv.org/html/1912.02263)

Audits using training prefixes whose next-item targets contributed to fitting measure training fit, including memorization, rather than held-out generalization. They can expose padding/readout errors, candidate-mask inconsistencies and failure to learn observed transitions; they cannot establish future recommendation quality or infer unobserved user traits. Interpretation: use such audits to motivate controlled experiments within the single GRU4Rec model—regularization, negative sampling or loss changes—then accept changes only through the fixed macro validation HR@10. Full-catalog training-prefix performance remains a diagnostic, not a replacement selection metric.
